content.comment_body: Hello, I am developing a hydraulic oil temperature monitoring system that activates cooling fans and notifies the operator if the oil overheats. The [product_name] base module offers analog input capabilities. Can anyone explain the pros and cons of using the base unit's analog input versus the separate [product_name] analog expansion module? Is there a difference in accuracy between the two?

The main difference is that the base module with analog inputs only accepts voltage signals within the 0-10V range. If you want to use current signals, you’ll need a resistor (e.g., 500 ohms) to convert current to voltage. The analog expansion module can handle both voltage signals (0-10V) and current signals (0/4-20mA) directly. Both have the same error limit: ±1.5% FS.
